why: When the title agreement rests on an Internal title -- a machine translation -- rather than on any real title, the pair may reach Review but not auto-accept unless an identity Alt ID agrees with no conflict (operator, 2026-10-02, accepting BMR-Review's proposal; scorer rule INTERNAL_TITLE_ACCEPT_REQUIRES_ALT_ID). A translated generic title matches unrelated works, and year, country and length corroborate weakly across a national cinema: with the discount at 0.8 and no such rule, this pair scored 80.2 Accept in BMR-Review's probe (length counts as a corroborator). Pending because with INTERNAL_TITLE_DISCOUNT absent the translation is not compared (title 0.33) and the field_quality_min below fails; it lands with the compare-spec version that adds the knob and the rule. Invariants are value-independent: the translation does carry the title (at least 0.5, so the pair is not passing merely because the title was ignored), and the verdict is not Accept. SCOPE: Basic, cross-language, Internal title on the submitted side, no Alt IDs; the Alt-ID release is pinned by BMR-Review's tests/test_internal_title_discount.py, not here.
